title: Final Answer
description: Essential Criteria: The response correctly identifies the observer's location as being on the equator.

title: Orbit Description
description: Essential Criteria: The response accurately describes the orbit of the space station as a geostationary orbit.

title: Centripetal Condition
description: Important Criteria: The response includes the reasoning that the gravitational force provides the necessary centripetal acceleration for the orbit.

title: Matching Periods
description: Important Criteria: The response explains that the orbital period of the space station must match the Earth's rotation period for it to remain above the same point.

title: Equatorial Requirement
description: Important Criteria: The response notes that the orbit must be equatorial for the satellite to stay directly above the observer.

title: Unit Consistency
description: Optional Criteria: The response checks that the units used for gravitational force and orbital radius are consistent.

title: Common Errors
description: Pitfall Criteria: The response avoids common errors such as misidentifying the observer's latitude or failing to mention the circular nature of the orbit.
